doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First instrument: a violin and lessons at home
summary: His parents bought him a violin and a teacher came to the house; he disliked practicing but it later helped with bass.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Right. But by my parents listening to classical music and religious music, they decided to get me a violin. That was my first thing about music. They got a violin for me. I started some lessons very, very young, but I didn’t stay with the instrument at all. But I did get a sense of the instrument, of what it was, and playing, but I didn’t particularly care for it. I didn’t like it.
Was this still in New Orleans?
You were first introduced to an instrument at that stage?

At a very early age, yeah. So here again it shows that my parents weren’t exactly poor, because I don’t know where it came from or who bought the instrument and all that, but you had to buy it, I’m sure . . .
. . . because nobody else was playing any instrument in my home at that time.

Yeah. I recall some lessons. Somebody came to the house. This is my best recollection of it at that time. They came to the house and [I would] take lessons, but I didn’t practice very much with it. I didn’t care much for practicing. But it stayed with me later on, when I started with the string bass, because actually a violin – the bass is just tuned – the strings are backwards – in other words, it’s E – A – D – G [on] the bass. The violin was just the opposite [g – d – a – e], but in a different clef. It was bass clef and then standard [treble clef].
